title: GPT-5.6 Sol Discovers Quasipolynomial Quantum Algorithm for Smooth-Modulus Vector Dihedral Coset Problem
whyItMatters: GPT-5.6 Sol discovered a quasipolynomial quantum sieving algorithm for the Vector Dihedral Coset Problem across arbitrary smooth moduli—breaking past the power-of-two modulus barrier in post-quantum cryptographic complexity.
summary: Posted to arXiv on November 13, 2026 (arXiv:2611.18857) by Aparna Gupte, this paper presents a quasipolynomial-time quantum algorithm for the Vector Dihedral Coset Problem (DCP) and the Extrapolated Dihedral Coset Problem (EDCP) for arbitrary B-smooth moduli—generalizing prior quasipolynomial results that had been restricted exclusively to power-of-two moduli (ASIACRYPT 2018, CRYPTO 2025). The author explicitly states that the core prime-factor sieving algorithm—which eliminates nonlinear phase terms modulo each prime factor p via Ivanyos–Santha diagonal-equation solving—was discovered in a July 2026 conversation with ChatGPT-5.6 Sol and subsequently improved with ChatGPT-6 Astra before full human verification and simplification.
technicalHighlights: Generalized quasipolynomial quantum DCP algorithms from power-of-two moduli to arbitrary B-smooth moduli with mixed prime factors.
Core prime-by-prime p-ary Fourier sieving algorithm discovered by GPT-5.6 Sol by coupling dihedral coset reduction with Ivanyos–Santha diagonal-equation subroutines.
Clarifies the exact sample-complexity boundary for post-quantum lattice cryptography: applies to EDCP with quasipolynomial samples while leaving standard polynomial-sample LWE unbroken.
caveats: Preprint undergoing community peer review (concurrent independent work by Boucher, Fouque, and Shen achieved related prime-power bounds); requires quasipolynomially many coset samples and does not break practical LWE lattice encryption.

scoreRationale.foundational: Advances Kuperberg-style hidden-shift quantum algorithms beyond power-of-two moduli to general smooth moduli.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly informs post-quantum security boundaries for dihedral-coset, group-action, and lattice-based cryptosystems.
scoreRationale.verification: Author-verified and simplified mathematical proof on arXiv, currently awaiting formal peer review.
scoreRationale.velocity: GPT-5.6 Sol autonomously synthesized the non-obvious cross-paper Ivanyos–Santha sieving reduction in interactive research sessions.
